body:
## Product overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD, design requirements, roadmap and themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for Unified Inference (Redwood product line). Unified Inference unifies hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes under a single developer API with consistent SLAs, predictable economics, and observable quality controls.

### Goals (high level)
- Provide a single API and operational model that guarantees consistent latency and cost characteristics across deployment modes.
- Reduce customer time-to-production by 30% year-over-year through improved onboarding, SDKs, and templates.
- Decrease 95th-percentile latency variance by 40% for common generation workloads via runtime optimizations and intelligent routing.
- Build pricing tiers and packaging that map to common customer segments (startup self-serve, mid-market reserved capacity, enterprise private deployments).

## Product Requirements (PRD)

### Problem statement
Customers manage complexity when moving from proof-of-concept to production due to divergent performance across model variants, lack of predictable latency under bursty traffic, and opaque unit economics for token-based billing. This causes missed SLOs and elevated costs.

### Target users
- ML engineers owning inference reliability and cost.
- Product engineers building chat, generation, and retrieval features.
- Platform teams standardizing inference across teams.

### Key features (MVP)
1. Unified REST/SDK API supporting text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with identical request/response shapes across deployment modes.
2. Model catalog with verified profiles (latency, cost-per-token, memory footprint) and recommended quantization variants.
3. Smart routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-aware) with automatic fallback to compatible variants.
4. Batching & KV cache controls per-route with configurable SLOs and autoscaling hints.
5. Pricing tiers and packaging: Self-serve hosted (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly/annual), Private (enterprise license + support).
6. Observability: per-request cost & latency breakdown, per-model dashboards, quality regression alerts tied to eval prompts.

### Acceptance criteria (list)
- API parity: same endpoints and response schemas for hosted, dedicated, and private.
- Performance: 99th percentile request latency <= 200ms for short-form generation (<=256 tokens) on hosted tier during baseline load.
- Cost transparency: token-level breakdown available in Console for 30-day windows.
- Rollout: canary and A/B rollout flows with automatic fallback configured in Console.
- Security: support for KMS/HSM key wrapping for Private deployments and RBAC for model access.

### Non-goals
- This PRD does not include custom model training pipelines. Model training and fine-tuning remain out-of-scope for Unified Inference 1.0.

## Design specifications (high level)

### Runtime & kernel selection
- Runtime will expose a cost-profile header per response: X-RW-CostProfile: {model_variant, quant, estimated_tokens, compute_ms}. (Note: header is JSON text string in responses).
- Kernel selector will map model architecture, sequence length distribution, and hardware sku to an execution profile. Profiles are stored in the model catalog as YAML entries (example below).

Example profile (text table):
| Field | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|
| model_variant | vicuna-13b-q4f16 | Quantized variant used for cost-first routing |
| target_skl | a100-80gb | Preferred hardware |
| seq_len_dist | p50:64,p95:320 | Typical sequence distribution observed |
| expected_latency_ms | 45 | Expected per-token compute time at baseline |

### API changes and compatibility
- Endpoints: POST /v1/generate, POST /v1/chat, POST /v1/embeddings, POST /v1/rerank.
- New query parameters: routing_policy (string), cache_key (string, optional), batching_hint (int, optional).
- Backward compatible: default routing_policy="latency-first" and batching_hint inferred from historical usage if omitted.

### Batching & cache controls
- Per-route config in Console: max_batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, kv_cache_ttl_secs.
- Default sensible values: max_batch_size=64, max_batch_latency_ms=15, kv_cache_ttl_secs=300.

### Observability contracts
- Metrics emitted: rw.requests, rw.tokens, rw.latency_ms.p50,p95,p99, rw.cache_hits, rw.batch_size_avg.
- Traces will include span tags: model_variant, quant, hardware_sku, route_id.

## Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters)

Themes by quarter (high-level):
- Q4 2028: GA of Unified Inference 1.0 — API parity, Console rollout, pricing tiers, initial Dedicated offering.
- Q1 2029: Improve routing heuristics (ML-based), adaptive batching, improved canary rollout automation.
- Q2 2029: Expanded model catalog (LLMs optimized for long context and multimodal), expanded regional footprints (APAC regions).
- Q3 2029: Private on-prem packaging and audit automation (SOC2+/ISO pipeline).
- Q4 2029: Redwood Optimize integration: per-customer cost recommendations and automated quantization suggestions.

Milestones (list):
- "2028-09-01: Public GA announcement and pricing publication" ,
- "2028-09-15: Console: per-route batching and cache controls shipped", 
- "2028-10-01: Dedicated: initial reserved capacity SKU available (r4/dk-1)",
- "2028-12-15: Private: first pilot customer deployment completed" 

## Pricing & packaging notes

Pricing philosophy:
- Map pricing to clear customer value: latency SLOs, reserved throughput, and data isolation carry a premium.
- Make self-serve attractive for SMBs while providing predictable committed pricing for enterprise customers.

Tier structure (summary):
1. Hosted (self-serve): pay-as-you-go per-token generation + per-1000-embedding units. Included: shared multi-tenant runtime, 30-day logs retention, community support.
   - Example list price: $0.0008 per generation token for base CPU-opt models; $0.0025 per generation token for high-performance GPU-backed variants.
2. Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commitment for GPU pools, lower per-token compute charge, SLA: 99.9% availability on reserved pools.
   - Example: 4x reserved nodes commit — $X/month + $0.0012/token compute charge. (Sales to finalize per-customer quotes).
3. Private (enterprise): annual license + support tiers, includes Private control plane, customer-managed VPC, HSM integrations, and extended audit retention.

Packaging guidance for sales:
- SMB: Start on Hosted; present quick ROI using sandbox prompts, show Console cost insights.
- Mid-market: Recommend Dedicated with 3-month ramp commit; provide pilot discount for the first quarter.
- Enterprise: Private deployment with SSO, KMS, and contractual SLAs. Offer on-prem packaging for highly regulated customers.

Migration notes (for customers moving between tiers):
1. Hosted -> Dedicated: export model pins and route configs; customer may opt for live cutover or blue-green.
2. Dedicated -> Private: coordinate data plane migration and KMS onboarding; expect 4-8 week deployment depending on networking approvals.

## Release notes (Q4 2028 GA)

Release: Unified Inference 1.0 (GA) — 2028-09-01
Highlights:
- Unified API (generate, chat, embeddings, rerank) across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
- Console: per-route batching and cache controls, cost & latency dashboards, rollout manager with canary/A-B support.
- Model catalog: verified performance profiles and recommended quantized variants.
- Smart routing: latency-first and cost-first policies with automatic fallback.
- Pricing: published Hosted and Dedicated entry pricing; Private packaging available via sales.

Notable fixes and caveats:
- Initial Dedicated SKUs limited to r4/dk-1 class hardware in NA and EU regions. APAC on roadmap for Q2 2029.
- Observability retention defaults to 30 days; extended retention is an add-on.
- Known issue: rare 95th-percentile latency spikes under highly adversarial prefix patterns — mitigation planned in Q1 2029 (adaptive batching).

Upgrade & migration checklist (numbered):
1. Run the migration readiness tool in Console to detect route-specific incompatibilities.
2. Pin model versions and export route config (JSON).
3. Create a canary route that mirrors production traffic at 1-5% for 24-72 hours.
4. Monitor rw.latency_ms.p95, rw.cache_hits, and model quality evals.
5. Promote route when metrics meet acceptance thresholds, or rollback via the Console rollout manager.

## Operational ownership & success metrics
- Product owner: Aisha Patel (product).
- Engineering lead: Liam Chen (eng-serving-runtime).
- SRE/ops: Maria Gomez (eng-sre).

Success metrics (90 days post-GA):

- 10 Dedicated contracts signed.
- Median p95 latency improvement target: baseline -> 40% reduction for short-form generation.
- Reduce average cost-per-1k-tokens by 15% for customers that adopt recommended quantized variants.
